Definition: plural of G2570 and G3040; Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete:--fair havens.
BiblicalUsage: Fair Havens is the bay on the south coast of Crete where Paul's ship put in on the voyage to Rome. The name promised more than the harbour gave: the crew wanted to winter somewhere better, sailed on, and met the storm.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Fair Havens warns me that a fair name is not a safe harbour. The sailors left a good anchorage for a better one and lost the ship — and I have learned to be thankful for the shelter God gives rather than always sailing on.
